ci_better_everyday.why: Your speed problem is a category problem: a shortboard can't make its own speed in weak waves. This is the small-wave workhorse answer — maximum paddle, maximum forgiveness, speed for free.
ci_better_everyday.advantage: Easiest wave-catching and the most forgiving ride of the three (paddling 5/5, forgiveness 4/5).
ci_better_everyday.tradeoff: The most board underfoot — turns are rounder and less snappy than the other two.

level_fit.note: At the entry of the board's range — accessible; upper-intermediate skill means it won't feel out of reach.

size_fit.note: 5'10" (34.5L) lands inside BOTH the volume and length windows — the cleanest size fit in the set.

ride_feel_fit.note: Low entry rocker (good for weak waves), single-to-double concave (speed), shortboard-familiar rails. Sketch-level read — labeled.

ci_g_skate.why: Fixes the category mismatch without giving up liveliness: it makes speed on flat sections — your exact frustration — and still turns like the boards you're used to.
ci_g_skate.advantage: The cleanest overall fit: only board with size inside both target windows, and the strongest ride-feel read.
ci_g_skate.tradeoff: Less pure paddle and forgiveness than the groveler (stability 3/5) — it asks a little more of you on the entry.

ci_two_happy.why: Stays in the shortboard family you know, but sized and shaped for real conditions — the 'keep the feel, fix the fit' path.
ci_two_happy.advantage: The most familiar ride of the three — your muscle memory transfers directly.
ci_two_happy.tradeoff: Weakest answer to truly gutless days — it still wants some push from the wave.
